greek: Καὶ ἐμνήσθη ὁ θεὸς τοῦ Νωε καὶ πάντων τῶν θηρίων καὶ πάντων τῶν κτηνῶν καὶ πάντων τῶν πετεινῶν καὶ πάντων τῶν ἑρπετῶν, ὅσα ἦν μετʼ αὐτοῦ ἐν τῇ κιβωτῷ, καὶ ἐπήγαγεν ὁ θεὸς πνεῦμα ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν, καὶ ἐκόπασεν τὸ ὕδωρ,
hint: God remembers Noah, and the wind that crosses the earth is the word of 1:2.

notes.text: μιμνήσκω is in the active *to remind*; its middle and passive, the form here and the verb as the New Testament uses it, *to remind oneself of, call to mind, remember*. The active glosses are left out, as for other verbs filed under their middle.
[[flag]] The Hebrew has *every living thing and all the cattle that were with him in the ark*. The Greek lists four kinds, adding the birds and the creeping things.
The word of 1:2, πνεῦμα θεοῦ, and the Hebrew is the word of 1:2 too, *rûaḥ*. Middle Liddell's first sense is *a blowing*; lower case, as there.
κοπάζω is *to grow weary*, and of the wind *to abate*. The Hebrew *wayyāšōkkû* is *subsided*.
Glossed again, first in this chapter.

reading: And [[reminded himself of|reminded himself of, called to mind, remembered, bethought himself of, was minded, bore in mind and did not forget]] — one completed act seen whole, not a process observed in progress — [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only]] of [[name:Νωε]] and [[of all|of all, of the whole, of every, of every single]] [[of the wild animals|of the wild animals, of the beasts, of the savage beasts, of the game]] and [[of all|of all, of the whole, of every, of every single]] [[of the flocks and herds|of the flocks and herds, of the single beasts, of the oxen, of the sheep, of the beasts for riding]] and [[of all|of all, of the whole, of every, of every single]] [[of the winged fowl|of the winged fowl, of the birds, of the able to fly and full fledged]] and [[of all|of all, of the whole, of every, of every single]] [[of the walking animals|of the walking animals, of the quadrupeds, of the creeping things, of the reptiles]], [[as great as|as great as, as much as, as far as, as long as, as many as]] was [[in the midst of|in the midst of, among, in common, along with, with, by means of]] him [[in the wooden box|within, inside of, and by means of the wooden box, the chest, the coffer]], and [[brought on|brought on, brought upon, set on and urged on, led on, brought in and invited, brought to, laid on and applied, brought forward, added]] [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only]] [[blowing|breath, wind, moving air, respiration, spirit]] [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near]] [[the earth|the land, the dry ground, the terrestrial realm]], and [[grew weary|grew weary, abated]] the water,

names.gloss: (Νωε, from Hebrew Nōaḥ, usually connected with nûaḥ, "to rest")

greek: καὶ ἐπεκαλύφθησαν αἱ πηγαὶ τῆς ἀβύσσου καὶ οἱ καταρράκται τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, καὶ συνεσχέθη ὁ ὑετὸς ἀπὸ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ.
hint: The springs and waterfalls are covered over, and the rain is held together.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *wayyissākĕrû*, *were stopped up*. The Greek has *were covered over*, ἐπικαλύπτω, the verb that covered the mountains at 7:19.
συνέχω is first *to hold together, keep together*, and in the passive *to be constrained*. The Hebrew *wayyikkālēʾ* is *was restrained*.

reading: and [[were covered over|were covered over, were covered up and shrouded, were put as a covering over]] [[the running waters|the running waters, the streams, the founts, the sources, the origins]] [[of the great deep|of the bottomless, of the depth without a floor to sound, of the unfathomable and unmeasurable deep]] and [[the broken waters|the broken waters, the waterfalls, the portcullises, the gulls]] [[of the heaven|of the heaven, of the vault, of the firmament and the sky]], and [[was held together|was held together, was kept together, was enclosed and encompassed and embraced, was kept from dispersing, was constrained and forced, was compressed and oppressed, was afflicted]] [[the rain|the rain, the heavy shower]] [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from]] [[of the heaven|of the heaven, of the vault, of the firmament and the sky]].

greek: καὶ ἐνεδίδου τὸ ὕδωρ πορευόμενον ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς, ἐνεδίδου καὶ ἠλαττονοῦτο τὸ ὕδωρ μετὰ πεντήκοντα καὶ ἑκατὸν ἡμέρας.
hint: The water gives way, going and giving way, for a hundred and fifty days.

notes.text: The Hebrew *wayyāšubû hammayim … hālôk wāšôb*, *the waters returned … going and returning*. The Greek keeps the doubling with a participle and the verb repeated: ἐνδίδωμι, *to give in, give way*, in the imperfect.
ἐλαττονόω is not in Middle Liddell; LSJ's one sense is *diminish*, citing this verse for the passive, so it is plain text.

reading: and [[was giving in|was giving in, was giving into hands and giving up to, was lending, was giving, was causing and exciting, was showing and exhibiting, was allowing and granting and conceding, was giving way, was yielding]] the water [[being driven|being driven, being carried, going, walking, marching, going across and passing]] [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from]] [[of the earth|of the land, of the dry ground, of the terrestrial realm]], [[was giving in|was giving in, was giving into hands and giving up to, was lending, was giving, was causing and exciting, was showing and exhibiting, was allowing and granting and conceding, was giving way, was yielding]] and was being diminished the water [[into the middle of|into the middle of, coming among, in pursuit and quest of, after]] fifty and a hundred [[days|days, day-breaks, times]].

greek: καὶ ἐκάθισεν ἡ κιβωτὸς ἐν μηνὶ τῷ ἑβδόμῳ, ἑβδόμῃ καὶ εἰκάδι τοῦ μηνός, ἐπὶ τὰ ὄρη τὰ Αραρατ.
hint: The box comes to rest on the twenty-seventh day, where the Hebrew has the seventeenth.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *bĕšibʿâ-ʿāśār yôm*, *on the seventeenth day*, as at 7:11, where the Greek also had the twenty-seventh.
καθίζω is first causal, *to make to sit down, seat*; *to sit down* is its later, intransitive use, which the verse has. The headword keeps the lexicon's order, as ὑπνόω did at 2:21.
*The mountains, those of Ararat*: the second article turns the name into a genitive modifier, the Hebrew *hārê ʾărārāṭ*.
Hebrew *ʾĂrārāṭ*.

reading: and [[made to sit down|made to sit down, seated, set and placed, encamped, set up, sat down and was seated and took its seat, settled and sank in]] — one completed act seen whole, not a process observed in progress — [[the wooden box|the wooden box, the chest, the coffer]] in month the seventh, seventh and twentieth of the month, [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near]] [[the mountains|the mountains, the hills]] the [[name:Αραρατ]].

names.gloss: (Αραρατ, from Hebrew ʾĂrārāṭ, the land the Assyrians called Urartu)

greek: τὸ δὲ ὕδωρ πορευόμενον ἠλαττονοῦτο ἕως τοῦ δεκάτου μηνός· ἐν δὲ τῷ ἑνδεκάτῳ μηνί, τῇ πρώτῃ τοῦ μηνός, ὤφθησαν αἱ κεφαλαὶ τῶν ὀρέων. —
hint: The mountain tops appear in the eleventh month in the Greek, the tenth in the Hebrew.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *bāʿăśîrî*, *in the tenth*: the waters decreased *until the tenth month*, and *in the tenth, on the first of the month*, the tops appeared. The Greek has the eleventh.
The aorist passive of ὁράω, *to see*: *were seen*.
Rahlfs prints a dash after the verse, closing a section.

reading: [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], the water [[being driven|being driven, being carried, going, walking, marching, going across and passing]] was being diminished [[until|until, till, while, so long as]] of the tenth month; in [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], the eleventh month, the first of the month, [[were seen|were seen, were looked at, were beheld and perceived and observed, were looked out for]] [[the heads|the heads, the whole persons, the lives, the tops, the sources, the crowns]] [[of the mountains|of the mountains, of the hills]].

greek: καὶ ἐγένετο μετὰ τεσσαράκοντα ἡμέρας ἠνέῳξεν Νωε τὴν θυρίδα τῆς κιβωτοῦ, ἣν ἐποίησεν,
hint: After forty days Noah opens the window.

notes.text: θυρίς, *a window*, one sense, so plain text; the Hebrew is *ḥallôn*.
With the double augment Rahlfs prints; ἀνοίγω, *to open*.

reading: and [[came into being|there came to be, there arose, there was brought into existence]] [[into the middle of|into the middle of, coming among, in pursuit and quest of, after]] forty [[days|days, day-breaks, times]] [[opened|opened, undid, laid open and unfolded and disclosed, got into the open sea]] [[name:Νωε]] the window [[of the wooden box|of the wooden box, of the chest, of the coffer]], which [[made|fashioned, wrought, produced]],

greek: καὶ ἀπέστειλεν τὸν κόρακα τοῦ ἰδεῖν εἰ κεκόπακεν τὸ ὕδωρ· καὶ ἐξελθὼν οὐχ ὑπέστρεψεν ἕως τοῦ ξηρανθῆναι τὸ ὕδωρ ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς.
hint: The Hebrew raven goes back and forth; the Greek raven does not return.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *wayyēṣēʾ yāṣôʾ wāšôb*, *it went out, going out and returning*, until the waters dried. The Greek has *did not return*, and adds *to see whether the water had grown weary*.
κόραξ, *a raven* or *carrion-crow*; the first tagged translation is *carrion-crow*.
Perfect of κοπάζω, *to grow weary*: the water standing abated.

reading: and [[sent off|sent off, sent away, banished, despatched, went away and departed]] [[the carrion-crow|the carrion-crow, the raven, the engine like a raven's beak for grappling ships, the hooked handle of a door, the instrument of torture]] [[to see|to see, to perceive, to behold, to look at]] if [[has grown weary|has grown weary and stands so, has abated and remains abated]] the water; and [[having gone out of|having gone out of, having come out, having gone away and marched off, having gone forth]] not [[turned round about|turned round about, turned back, turned about and turned short round, returned, turned away and eluded]] [[until|until, till, while, so long as]] [[to be parched up|to be parched up, to be dried up, to become dry and be parched, to be laid dry]] the water [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from]] [[of the earth|of the land, of the dry ground, of the terrestrial realm]].

greek: καὶ ἀπέστειλεν τὴν περιστερὰν ὀπίσω αὐτοῦ ἰδεῖν εἰ κεκόπακεν τὸ ὕδωρ ἀπὸ προσώπου τῆς γῆς·
hint: The dove is sent after the raven, where the Hebrew sends it from Noah.

notes.text: [[flag]] *After it*, the raven. The Hebrew is *mēʾittô*, *from with him*, from Noah.
περιστερά, *the common pigeon*, then *dove*: the bird of the Spirit's descent in all four Gospels.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus leaves out προσώπου, as Rahlfs's apparatus records.

reading: and [[sent off|sent off, sent away, banished, despatched, went away and departed]] [[the common pigeon|the common pigeon, the dove]] [[after|after, backwards, back and back again, again, hereafter, behind]] him [[to see|to see, to perceive, to behold, to look at]] if [[has grown weary|has grown weary and stands so, has abated and remains abated]] the water [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from]] [[face|face, visage, countenance, look, outward appearance]] [[of the earth|of the land, of the dry ground, of the terrestrial realm]];

greek: καὶ οὐχ εὑροῦσα ἡ περιστερὰ ἀνάπαυσιν τοῖς ποσὶν αὐτῆς ὑπέστρεψεν πρὸς αὐτὸν εἰς τὴν κιβωτόν, ὅτι ὕδωρ ἦν ἐπὶ παντὶ προσώπῳ πάσης τῆς γῆς, καὶ ἐκτείνας τὴν χεῖρα αὐτοῦ ἔλαβεν αὐτὴν καὶ εἰσήγαγεν αὐτὴν πρὸς ἑαυτὸν εἰς τὴν κιβωτόν.
hint: The dove finds no rest for her feet: ἀνάπαυσις, a word from the root of rest.

notes.text: The Hebrew is *mānôaḥ lĕkap-raglāh*, *a resting place for the sole of her foot*: *mānôaḥ* is from *nûaḥ*, the root of Noah's name. ἀνάπαυσις, *repose, rest*, is from ἀναπαύω, as διαναπαύσει at 5:29 was.

notes.lemma: ἐπὶ παντὶ προσώπῳ πάσης τῆς γῆς
notes.text: The Hebrew *ʿal-pĕnê kol-hāʾāreṣ* has *face*, and so does the Greek, which adds παντί.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus reads ἀνέστρεψεν.

reading: and not [[having found|having found, having found out, having discovered, having gotten and gained]] [[the common pigeon|the common pigeon, the dove]] [[repose|repose, rest, relaxation and recreation, rest from]] [[to the feet|to the feet, to the talons, to the feet of a hill]] of her [[turned round about|turned round about, turned back, turned about and turned short round, returned, turned away and eluded]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward]] him [[into|into, to, in, rest in]] [[the wooden box|the wooden box, the chest, the coffer]], [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as]] water was [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near]] [[all|all, the whole, every, every single]] [[face|face, visage, countenance, look, outward appearance]] [[of all|of all, of the whole, of every, of every single]] [[of the earth|of the land, of the dry ground, of the terrestrial realm]], and [[having stretched out|having stretched out, having spread out, having put forth]] [[the hand|the hand, the hand and arm, the arm]] of him [[took|took, received, took hold of and grasped and seized]] her and [[led in|led in, led into and introduced, admitted, imported, called in, brought in and brought forward]] her [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward]] himself [[into|into, to, in, rest in]] [[the wooden box|the wooden box, the chest, the coffer]].

greek: καὶ ἐπισχὼν ἔτι ἡμέρας ἑπτὰ ἑτέρας πάλιν ἐξαπέστειλεν τὴν περιστερὰν ἐκ τῆς κιβωτοῦ·
hint: Noah waits seven more days, in the lexicon's words, 'having held upon'.

notes.text: ἐπέχω is first *to have* or *hold upon*; *to stay, stop, wait, pause* is its fourth sense, which the verse means. The Hebrew *wayyāḥel* is *he waited*.
πάλιν is first *back, backwards*, and *again, anew* later in the entry.

reading: and [[having held upon|having held upon, having held out and presented and offered, having directed towards and aimed at, having intended and purposed, having faced, having kept in and held back and checked, having stayed and stopped and waited and paused, having reached and extended over]] [[yet|yet, as yet, still, further, besides, moreover]] [[days|days, day-breaks, times]] seven [[other|other, the other of two, another, second, other than usual and different]] [[back|back, backwards, again and once more and anew, again in turn]] [[sent quite away|sent quite away, dispatched]] [[the common pigeon|the common pigeon, the dove]] [[out of|out of, forth from, from]] [[of the wooden box|of the wooden box, of the chest, of the coffer]];

greek: καὶ ἀνέστρεψεν πρὸς αὐτὸν ἡ περιστερὰ τὸ πρὸς ἑσπέραν καὶ εἶχεν φύλλον ἐλαίας κάρφος ἐν τῷ στόματι αὐτῆς, καὶ ἔγνω Νωε ὅτι κεκόπακεν τὸ ὕδωρ ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς.
hint: The Hebrew olive leaf is freshly plucked; the Greek one is a dry stalk.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *wĕhinnēh ʿălēh-zayit ṭārāp bĕpîhā*, *and behold, a freshly plucked olive leaf in her mouth*. The Greek has no *behold*, and for *freshly plucked* has κάρφος, *a dry stalk*, *dry twigs*, such as birds build nests of.
ἀναστρέφω is first *to turn upside down, upset*; *to turn back, return* is its second sense.
*Toward evening*, the article with a prepositional phrase; the Hebrew *lĕʿēt ʿereb*.

reading: and [[turned upside down|turned upside down, upset, turned back and brought back, rallied, turned back and returned and retired, dwelt, conducted herself, revolved, faced about]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward]] him [[the common pigeon|the common pigeon, the dove]] the [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward]] [[evening|evening, eventide, eve, nightfall, the west]] and [[was having|was having, was holding, was possessing, was keeping, was holding fast, was bearing up against and supporting]] [[leaf|leaf, foliage, petal, herb]] [[of olive-tree|of olive-tree, of olives, of the fruit of the olive-tree and olive]] [[a dry stalk|a dry stalk, dry sticks, dry twigs and chips and straws and bits of wool]] [[in the mouth|within, inside of, and by means of the mouth, the mouth as the organ of speech, the mouthpiece, the face, the chasm and cleft]] of her, and [[learned to know|learned to know, perceived, marked, learned, discerned and distinguished]] [[name:Νωε]] [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as]] [[has grown weary|has grown weary and stands so, has abated and remains abated]] the water [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from]] [[of the earth|of the land, of the dry ground, of the terrestrial realm]].

greek: καὶ ἐπισχὼν ἔτι ἡμέρας ἑπτὰ ἑτέρας πάλιν ἐξαπέστειλεν τὴν περιστεράν, καὶ οὐ προσέθετο τοῦ ἐπιστρέψαι πρὸς αὐτὸν ἔτι. —
hint: The dove does not come back again.

notes.text: *Did not put to returning*: προστίθημι with an infinitive for doing a thing again, the Hebraism of 4:2, *wĕlōʾ-yāsĕpâ šûb*.
Rahlfs prints a dash after the verse, closing a section.

reading: and [[having held upon|having held upon, having held out and presented and offered, having directed towards and aimed at, having intended and purposed, having faced, having kept in and held back and checked, having stayed and stopped and waited and paused, having reached and extended over]] [[yet|yet, as yet, still, further, besides, moreover]] [[days|days, day-breaks, times]] seven [[other|other, the other of two, another, second, other than usual and different]] [[back|back, backwards, again and once more and anew, again in turn]] [[sent quite away|sent quite away, dispatched]] [[the common pigeon|the common pigeon, the dove]], and not [[put to|put to, handed over and delivered, gave and bestowed, imposed further, attributed, added]] [[to turn about|to turn about, to turn round, to return, to turn towards, to correct and make to repent]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward]] him [[yet|yet, as yet, still, further, besides, moreover]].

greek: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ ἑνὶ καὶ ἑξακοσιοστῷ ἔτει ἐν τῇ ζωῇ τοῦ Νωε, τοῦ πρώτου μηνός, μιᾷ τοῦ μηνός, ἐξέλιπεν τὸ ὕδωρ ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς· καὶ ἀπεκάλυψεν Νωε τὴν στέγην τῆς κιβωτοῦ, ἣν ἐποίησεν, καὶ εἶδεν ὅτι ἐξέλιπεν τὸ ὕδωρ ἀπὸ προσώπου τῆς γῆς.
hint: The water leaves the earth on the first day of the year.

notes.text: [[flag]] Not in the Hebrew of this verse, which has *in the six hundred and first year, in the first month, on the first of the month*. The Greek repeats the phrase of 7:11.
[[flag]] The Hebrew is *ḥārĕbû hammayim*, *the waters dried*. ἐκλείπω is first *to leave out, omit*, then *to forsake*, and intransitively *to fail, cease*.
The Hebrew is *wayyāsar … ʾet-miksēh hattēbâ*, *removed the covering of the ark*. ἀποκαλύπτω, *to uncover*, the verb of revelation in the New Testament; στέγη, *a roof*.

notes.lemma: εἶδεν ὅτι ἐξέλιπεν τὸ ὕδωρ ἀπὸ προσώπου τῆς γῆς
notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *wĕhinnēh ḥārĕbû pĕnê hāʾădāmâ*, *and behold, the face of the ground was dry*. The Greek has *that the water had left off from the face of the earth*.

reading: and [[came into being|there came to be, there arose, there was brought into existence]] in the [[one|one, a single one, one alone]] and six hundredth year [[in the life|within, inside of, and by means of the life, the means of life and substance, existence, a way of life]] of [[name:Νωε]], of the first month, [[one|one, a single one, one alone]] of the month, [[left out|left out, omitted and passed over, forsook and deserted and abandoned, suffered an eclipse, died, left off and ceased and stopped, failed and was wanting]] the water [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from]] [[of the earth|of the land, of the dry ground, of the terrestrial realm]]; and [[uncovered|uncovered, disclosed and revealed, revealed his whole mind]] [[name:Νωε]] [[the roof|the roof, the roofed place, the chamber and room, the tent]] [[of the wooden box|of the wooden box, of the chest, of the coffer]], which [[made|fashioned, wrought, produced]], and [[saw|saw, perceived, beheld, looked at]] [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as]] [[left out|left out, omitted and passed over, forsook and deserted and abandoned, suffered an eclipse, died, left off and ceased and stopped, failed and was wanting]] the water [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from]] [[face|face, visage, countenance, look, outward appearance]] [[of the earth|of the land, of the dry ground, of the terrestrial realm]].

greek: ἐν δὲ τῷ μηνὶ τῷ δευτέρῳ, ἑβδόμῃ καὶ εἰκάδι τοῦ μηνός, ἐξηράνθη ἡ γῆ.
hint: In the Greek, the earth is dry a year to the day after the flood began.

notes.text: The twenty-seventh, as in the Hebrew here. The Greek began the flood on the twenty-seventh of the second month (7:11), so its flood lasts a year to the day; the Hebrew began it on the seventeenth, and lasts a year and ten days.
ξηραίνω, *to parch up, dry up*, in the passive; the entry's own *to become dry* is in the chain.

reading: in [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], the month the second, seventh and twentieth of the month, [[was parched up|was parched up, was dried up, became dry and was parched, was laid dry]] [[the earth|the land, the dry ground, the terrestrial realm]].

greek: Καὶ εἶπεν κύριος ὁ θεὸς τῷ Νωε λέγων
hint: God speaks to Noah.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew has *ʾĕlōhîm*, *God*; the Greek adds κύριος.

reading: And [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told]] [[lord|lord, master, the one having power and authority over]] [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only]] to [[name:Νωε]] [[saying|saying, speaking, declaring, calling by name, telling]]

greek: Ἔξελθε ἐκ τῆς κιβωτοῦ, σὺ καὶ ἡ γυνή σου καὶ οἱ υἱοί σου καὶ αἱ γυναῖκες τῶν υἱῶν σου μετὰ σοῦ
hint: Go out of the box, you and your house.

notes.text: The imperative of ἐξέρχομαι, the verb of 4:16.

reading: [[go out of|go out of, come out, go away and march off, go forth]] [[out of|out of, forth from, from]] [[of the wooden box|of the wooden box, of the chest, of the coffer]], you and [[the woman|the woman, the mistress and lady, the wife and spouse]] of you and the sons of you and [[the women|the women, the mistresses and ladies, the wives and spouses, the mortal women]] of the sons of you [[in the midst of|in the midst of, among, in common, along with, with, by means of]] you

greek: καὶ πάντα τὰ θηρία, ὅσα ἐστὶν μετὰ σοῦ, καὶ πᾶσα σὰρξ ἀπὸ πετεινῶν ἕως κτηνῶν, καὶ πᾶν ἑρπετὸν κινούμενον ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἐξάγαγε μετὰ σεαυτοῦ· καὶ αὐξάνεσθε καὶ πληθύνεσθε ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς.
hint: 'Increase and multiply': the blessing of 1:22 and 1:28, now addressed to the creatures.

notes.text: The words of the blessing at 1:22 and 1:28. [[flag]] The Hebrew here is third person, *that they may swarm on the earth and be fruitful and multiply*; the Greek has the second person and no *swarm*.

notes.lemma: πάντα τὰ θηρία … καὶ πᾶσα σάρξ … καὶ πᾶν ἑρπετόν
notes.text: Nominative, continuing the list of those told to go out at 8:16; ἐξάγαγε then takes them up.
Both the first sense in the passive: αὐξάνω, *to make large, increase*, and πληθύνω, *to make full, increase, multiply*. The entry's passive glosses, *to grow* and *to prevail*, are in the chains.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus reads σου.

hint: Noah builds an altar and offers whole burnt-offerings.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *mizbēaḥ laYHWH*, *an altar to YHWH*; the Greek has τῷ θεῷ. θυσιαστήριον, *an altar*, one sense, is plain text: the place of θυσία, the offering of 4:3.

The Hebrew is *ʿōlōt*, *burnt-offerings*. ὁλοκάρπωσις is in neither Middle Liddell nor LSJ; LSJ has the verb ὁλοκαρπόομαι, *to be offered as a whole burnt-offering*. It stands as plain text, *whole burnt-offerings*. [[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus reads the singular.
ἀναφέρω is first *to bring* or *carry up*; *to offer* comes later in the entry.

greek: καὶ ὠσφράνθη κύριος ὁ θεὸς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας, καὶ εἶπεν κύριος ὁ θεὸς διανοηθείς Οὐ προσθήσω ἔτι τοῦ καταράσασθαι τὴν γῆν διὰ τὰ ἔργα τῶν ἀνθρώπων, ὅτι ἔγκειται ἡ διάνοια τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐπιμελῶς ἐπὶ τὰ πονηρὰ ἐκ νεότητος· οὐ προσθήσω οὖν ἔτι πατάξαι πᾶσαν σάρκα ζῶσαν, καθὼς ἐποίησα.
hint: The 'sweet smell' Paul uses of Christ's offering in Ephesians 5:2.

notes.text: The phrase of Ephesians 5:2, παρέδωκεν ἑαυτὸν … θυσίαν τῷ θεῷ εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας, and Philippians 4:18. [[flag]] The Hebrew is *rêaḥ hannîḥōaḥ*, *the soothing smell*, from *nûaḥ*, the root of Noah's name; εὐωδία, *a sweet smell*, one sense, loses the root.
[[flag]] The Hebrew is *wayyōʾmer YHWH ʾel-libbô*, *YHWH said to his heart*. The Greek has *having been minded*, διανοέομαι, the verb of 6:6, and adds ὁ θεός.
[[flag]] The Hebrew is *baʿăbûr hāʾādām*, *because of man*. The Greek adds *the works* and makes the men plural.

notes.lemma: ἔγκειται ἡ διάνοια τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐπιμελῶς ἐπὶ τὰ πονηρά
notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *yēṣer lēb hāʾādām raʿ*, *the inclination of man's heart is evil*. The Greek repeats its words of 6:5, ἐπιμελῶς ἐπὶ τὰ πονηρά, with διάνοια, *thought*, and ἔγκειμαι, *to lie in, be involved in*.
Middle Liddell gives καθώς first as *= καθά*, *according as*, then *how*.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

hint: Summer and spring, where the Hebrew has summer and winter.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *qayiṣ wāḥōrep*, *summer and winter*. The Greek has ἔαρ, *spring*.
The Hebrew *lōʾ yišbōtû*, *shall not cease*, from *šābat*. The Greek has καταπαύω, the verb of 2:2–3, where God rested on the seventh day, and the Hebrew there is *šābat* too.
The Hebrew has *ʿōd*, *yet, while*: *while all the days of the earth remain*. The Greek has the days alone, in the accusative of time.
